answer: A Sybil defense can run on lighthouse beacons: each account keeps a beacon whose signal fades unless rekindled by a distinct human encounter, so standing tracks lived presence, not account count. When a comet passes, each beacon must flash a one-time pattern drawn from the comet's trail; only beacons watched by neighbors are confirmed. Sybil fleets fail because one operator cannot be in many places at once: cloned beacons flash identical patterns, betraying their shared origin, and unattended beacons dim. Flashing costs stored light, so forgery burns the attacker's standing.
